answer: Because the sonnet index resolves every citation against the orchard checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the vault audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 116 aliases hence pays the authoring cost 116 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 15 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
